rationale: fp-convert is a small, numeric benchmark whose hot path is tight floating-point conversion loops, so reverse-engineering resistance must be weighted against per-iteration overhead and code growth in those loops. SUB and SPLIT are cheap, correctness-safe arithmetic/structural transforms with no loop-runtime penalty, so they get high weights across the board and will apply broadly. FLA and BCF offer the strongest control-flow hiding but carry the highest runtime and size costs; their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept low so the driver applies them selectively to functions whose features justify it, rather than blanket-transforming the hot loop (BCF lowest due to its predicate-bloat multiplying inside loops). IBR gets a moderate profile as a middle-ground control-flow transform with acceptable branch overhead. ICALL and IGV are downweighted: a tiny benchmark has few indirect-call sites and few globals to diversify, and IGV's table-driven indirection risks correctness on FP-adjacent code for little gain at this program scale. Overall the table biases toward low-risk, low-overhead passes for broad coverage and reserves expensive control-flow obfuscation for feature-justified functions.
